records.our_prose: St. George's low-elevation Dixie belt (Mojave-edge high desert) runs slicing cucumbers on one spring cycle only, per USU Extension's Suggested Vegetable Planting Dates for Utah. Direct-sow around March 15, the Group C (Tender) date for St. George, about two weeks ahead of the March 30 average last frost; the table's explicit local date runs earlier than a generic frost-relative rule would. Harvest begins about 63 days later, around May 17, and continues into late June. Once St. George's daytime highs push past 95°F and the county's own frost-and-elevation data show summer highs routinely reaching 100°F in June through August, vines stop setting fruit and any that does form turns bitter. USU documents fall planting for cool-season crops in the St. George area but gives no fall or summer-replant window for slicing cucumbers, so there is no second cycle here; frost returns around November 1, well after the plants have already stopped producing for the year.
